description_full: DRDGOLD Limited, a gold mining company, engages in the extraction of gold from the retreatment of surface mine tailings in South Africa. The company was formerly known as Durban Roodepoort Deep Limited and changed its name to DRDGOLD Limited in 2004. The company was incorporated in 1895 and is headquartered in Johannesburg, South Africa. DRDGOLD Limited is a subsidiary of Sibanye Gold Proprietary Limited.
ceo_bio: Mr. Daniel Johannes Pretorius B.Proc., L.L.M., LLB | CEO & Executive Director | Age 58 | Compensation: $1.3M (FY2026)
financial_summary: DRDGOLD Limited is a small-cap basic materials business with a $1.7B market cap on $441M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +8% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +7.0pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 39% against a 9% cost of capital — a 30-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 29%.

The business throws off $70M in free cash flow — roughly 16 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.57× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 1.4%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 2.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 37% operating margin runs 28pp above the Basic Materials median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 2.84x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+10.6% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 222 companies in the universe; the top four hold 25% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are roughly flat over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 49% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 58% and a beta of 0.78, it is more defensive than the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 1.31 vs 5y 0.56), so read it loosely.
About $6.2M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 47% in the 2020 crash, 52% in the 2022 bear market and 77% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $16.05 (margin of safety -25%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 17%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $12.91 to $20.23 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Basic Materials peers: P/E 6.9 vs 14.2 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 3% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 4.0% (below the risk-free rate).
The Street target $35.00 on average, 75% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 39% clears the cost of capital of 9.0% by 30pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.55).
It runs a 29% gross margin and converts 16% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.57x.
ROE of 27% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.4x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 12pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $69.3M.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 7.8, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 8.1% over 3 years and 10.0% over 5 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 17%).
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 30.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 2.5% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Analysts expect -9.8% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.1%), and institutions hold 9%.
Insider trading is two-way: 1 purchase and 6 sales over the past year, net $395K sold.
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.4% (5.1% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 18 consecutive years, raising it 48.4% a year over the last five.
